requirement:
Markdown reports only `Comment` attachments. Each HTML comment block whose
trimmed text starts with `<!--` and ends with `-->` is one attachment.
An inline HTML comment within a paragraph remains paragraph text, and
comment delimiters inside fenced code remain code.
rationale:
The subject is covered by the `test.md` case in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]`. That test carries a `{test}` reference to `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.attachments`. I did not need to request any implementation source. Obligations and the test scenarios that check them: - **Only `Comment` attachments.** The test compares the full list of `(kind, text)` pairs for the file against the expected list. Every expected entry has kind `Comment`, so any `Annotation` or other kind in Markdown output would fail the comparison. - **Each HTML comment block is one attachment.** The source has a single-line block, ``. It also has a multi-line block, ``. The expected result has exactly those two attachments, with the multi-line one as a single attachment whose span covers both lines. - **Trimmed text starts with ``.** Two negative cases cover this. A non-comment HTML block, `
html
`, is not reported. An unterminated block, ` word.` is not reported, because it is absent from the expected list. - **Comment delimiters inside fenced code remain code.** The fenced `html` block containing `` is not reported. The assertion is an exact equality on the attachment list (kind plus span text, sorted by span start), so extra or missing attachments would fail it. Together these scenarios cover each clause and each negative case the requirement names. I found no gap. Mixed HTML blocks, such as a comment followed by other markup in the same block, are edge cases the requirement text does not name.
